name: Integral nationalism
summary: Integral nationalism, as theorized by Charles Maurras for Action Francaise, holds that the nation is the supreme political value, above individuals, classes and humanitarian aims. It is counter-revolutionary: it blames republican democracy and party rule for national decline and proposes a traditional, hereditary, anti-parliamentary and decentralized monarchy, supported by Catholicism as social cement and by corporate class collaboration. It excludes groups it treats as Anti-France (Protestants, Jews, Freemasons, foreigners) and accepts force and a coup to restore authority.
scope: The French strand of Charles Maurras and Action Francaise (c. 1899 to 1945), based on Maurras's Enquete sur la monarchie and the scholarly accounts of the movement. It excludes later variants such as Ukrainian OUN nationalism, Salazarism and Francoism, which borrowed from it but differ in religion, violence and regime form.

sources.usedFor: Movement practice: federal monarchy, corporatism, Camelots du Roi, coup strategy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Maurras's social thought leaned toward La Tour du Pin's paternal social Catholicism; state health insurance is not addressed, so adherents are split on it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage law is not a documented concern; national solidarity under the king suggests sympathy for workers but also opposition to state class legislation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Maurras did not condemn the bourgeoisie but put national interest above economics; markets are subordinate to the nation, so mild disagreement is inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the sources favors nationalization; the doctrine stresses organic bodies and corporations over state ownership, so this is inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented stance; paternal solidarity pulls one way and defense of property and the bourgeoisie the other.

unions-good.rationale: Maurras criticized labor laws that made class conflict inevitable, favouring corporate bodies uniting employers and workers rather than class unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Maurras did not attack the bourgeoisie and defended property as part of the organic social order, though always subordinate to the nation; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; national interest could justify regulation, but the doctrine is not anti-business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; paternalist social Catholicism opposes both abolition of aid and state dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Integral nationalism rejects class-based revolutionary syndicalism in favour of national solidarity and corporations; inferred opposition to worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Maurras accepted emergency authority and wartime censorship as necessary and put state security first; inferred approval of surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Moral order and authority are central; liberal drug policy is inferred to be opposed as individualist decadence.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Maurras himself was convicted for inciting violence and vilified groups; adherents reject liberal speech-restriction framed around minorities, though they favour censorship of enemies of the nation.

strong-leader.rationale: Maurras wanted authority at the top and praised wartime dictatorship, but his ideal was a hereditary king rather than an improvised strongman.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine is built on strong national authority; Maurras opposed centralization but never the state itself, praising the monarchy as guardian of the nation.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; order and a strong state versus the armed-nation tradition leave this open.

empower-police-military.rationale: Maurras blamed the republic for neglecting army, navy and intelligence services and demanded authority and defense preparedness.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Catholic-influenced moral order and social discipline make legalization unlikely to be supported; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Maurras advocated decentralization under a federal monarchy and favored local and corporate bodies, while keeping a strong central power for national matters.

rehabilitation.rationale: The emphasis on authority and order suggests punishment over rehabilitation; no direct statement.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is one of the organic units Maurras treated as foundations of the nation, and he praised Catholic rural family life as a source of renewal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The traditionalist, Catholic-cultural order Maurras defended implies opposition; inferred from his family and moral doctrine.

abortion-legal.rationale: Maurras blamed the republic for falling birth rates and stressed national demographic strength; opposition is inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Maurras backed Catholicism as the national religion for its social cohesion, though he was personally agnostic and valued it politically.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Integral nationalism puts the nation above group claims and humanitarian aims; inferred opposition to group-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditionalist organic-order thinking treats sex roles as natural; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending the national tradition and the political and cultural order inherited from the old France is the core of the doctrine.

gradual-change.rationale: It is counter-revolutionary and respects historical institutions, but also openly sought a coup to restore the monarchy.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Maurras excluded foreigners (metics) as part of Anti-France who could never be integrated, implying restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The nation is the highest value; supranational authority over it contradicts the doctrine, though Maurras pursued alliances.

free-trade.rationale: National interest is placed over economic liberalism; inferred preference for protecting national interests.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is held above individual, class and humanitarian interests; this is the defining principle.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Humanitarian concerns rank below national interest, so adherents reject interventions for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Maurras treated foreigners as unassimilable elements of Anti-France; borders open to all are irreconcilable with the doctrine.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; anti-liberal but nationalist power concerns favor growth, inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The doctrine predates climate concerns and has no stated position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Willpower over reason and traditionalism imply scepticism of progress as a cure, inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; national power and independence are favoured, inferred support for nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Counter-revolutionary, though it sought a royalist coup d'etat to overthrow the Republic, so not wholly opposed to extra-legal change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Maurras held national existence should be judged by reasoning patriots rather than voted on, favouring elite competence over mass opinion.

central-planning.rationale: Corporate and organic social bodies are preferred to state planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Class-based worker or public ownership schemes conflict with national solidarity; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Maurras wrote nothing on land taxation, and the doctrine gives no principle that decides it, so adherents are split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family continuity and inheritance underpin the traditional order; inferred opposition.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; unconditional state payments conflict with the organic corporate social order, inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: National interest over economic liberalism suggests protectionism; inferred rather than documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; national power favours it but decentralization and corporate autonomy oppose state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Social Catholic thinking in the La Tour du Pin line favoured rooted property and family-held farms; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejects revolutionary syndicalism and class-struggle visions; the bourgeoisie is not condemned.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No stated view; abolition of national monetary institutions runs against nationalist state power.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Action Francaise espoused corporatism, organizing employers and workers in bodies replacing class conflict.

one-party-rule.rationale: Maurras opposed party rule, which he identified with the Republic's rule of party interest over the national interest; he preferred a hereditary king above parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maurras's Enquete argues for a traditional, hereditary, anti-parliamentary, decentralized monarchy as the only regime serving the nation.

democracy-best.rationale: Maurras rejected democratic principles as contrary to natural inequality and blamed democracy for national decline.

direct-votes.rationale: Maurras held national existence should not be put to a vote; direct democracy epitomizes the rule of numbers he attacked.

workers-councils.rationale: A class-based council basis for power contradicts national solidarity and royal authority.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nation is an indivisible organic unity, though local liberties are defended within it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maurras held that democracy contradicts natural inequality and supported hereditary authority and a hierarchical order.

political-violence-never.rationale: Action Francaise's Camelots du Roi engaged in street violence and the movement sought a coup, so adherents reject pacifism about politics.

war-builds-character.rationale: Willpower and national vitality are praised, but Maurras's own foreign policy was defensive revanche against Germany; adherents differ.

separate-church-state.rationale: Maurras criticized state secularism for denying religion a national role, and Action Francaise backed Catholicism as state religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as social mortar but distrusted the Gospels and appealed to natural law and classical values, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defense and justice are functions of national authority; private provision is incompatible with a strong state.

military-superiority.rationale: Maurras attacked republican disarmament and demanded strong army, navy and intelligence against Germany.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Maurras favoured state antisemitism over scientific racism, defining the nation by historical culture and tradition rather than biology, but excluded Jews and foreigners as unassimilable.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Integral nationalism puts the nation above class and promotes national solidarity against class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Natural inequality is accepted and hierarchy defended.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; national sovereignty over territory is paramount, inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Maurras opposed assimilation and dismantling the empire; reparations to former colonies would contradict national interest.

civilizational-union.rationale: Maurras was nation-centred and anti-universalist; unions of civilizations would dissolve the nation, though alliances were accepted.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Maurras blamed democratic individualism for each person pursuing his own interest and disorder.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The nation outranks the individual; organic units and obligations take precedence over individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lie outside Maurras's concerns, though he valued rural France; no position can be inferred with confidence.

limit-population.rationale: Maurras lamented the republic's falling birth rate and treated demographic strength as a national interest.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Traditionalist but nationalist and power-oriented; not anti-industrial, inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Prefers continuity and established institutions; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Traditionalist moral order implies opposition; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Authority is personal and hereditary, tradition-based; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Strong authority over security matters; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine seeks to restore the constitutional, political and cultural order of the Ancien Regime.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Maurras claimed empirical method (politique d'abord, necessary realities) but remained dogmatically monarchist and nationalist.

direct-action.rationale: Action Francaise used street leagues and planned a coup, yet also contested elections and wrote journalism.

means-match-ends.rationale: Its methods (street violence, coup) were meant to restore authority, not to prefigure the future order.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the doctrine of civilization, tradition and national greatness.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Organic hierarchical order with differentiated roles and corporations.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rejects communist egalitarian distribution under natural inequality and hierarchy.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of socialism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Maurras did not condemn the bourgeoisie systematically and preached class collaboration.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class power contradicts national solidarity and monarchic authority.

collective-farming.rationale: Favoured rooted family farming and rural traditional life.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist class analysis is rejected; Maurras located war risk in republican weakness.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is legitimate and national defense requires taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal individualism is rejected; the state may enforce moral and national order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The nation outranks individuals, and rights attach to organic units like families, provinces, corporations.

conscription.rationale: National defense is paramount; Maurras faulted republican neglect of military strength.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Belonging to the nation is organic and not a market choice.

state-as-business.rationale: The state embodies the national interest, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; social Catholic paternalism sympathetic but liberty talk rejected as republican slogan.

media-academia-power.rationale: Maurras attacked intellectual and press elites of the Republic and L'Avenir de l'intelligence argued about elites; inferred agreement.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Maurras backed state antisemitism over scientific racism, so he did not rest on genetic claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Maurras favoured local and corporate representation over national democracy, defending families, provinces and corporations.

total-state.rationale: He wanted strong authority at the top but criticized the state acting as sole arbiter and favoured decentralization and autonomous bodies.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement's premise is national decline under the Republic and renewal through restoration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Maurras opposed republican colonial expansion as diverting from revenge against Germany but opposed decolonization, so expansion is not a central aim.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Royal allegiance matters but the system is a nation-state monarchy, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; rural traditional life is praised but serfdom is not advocated.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Maurras appealed to reason, natural law and classical values rather than power-relative truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Appeals to natural law and classical values, yet Maurras was an agnostic positivist valuing nation-specific tradition; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Maurras opposed party interests as rule against national interest and held that a single national interest guides policy under the king.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Maurras excluded Jews as Anti-France; a Jewish state is not addressed, inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Maurras's sources never discuss diaspora return, and nation-first thinking could cut either way (co-nationals yes, outsiders no).

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras favored classical French and Provencal regionalism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Employer and worker partnership through corporations rather than democratic votes in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic schooling preference pulls for, state curriculum against.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not a theme of Maurrasian doctrine, which put national power and authority above economic technique.

economic-freedom.rationale: National interest subordinated economics; liberalism rejected.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; the king as symbol, but laws and authority emphasized.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nation is the highest value and the sovereign unit, though the principle is applied to France primarily.

force-without-un.rationale: Nation-first; supranational approval is not required, inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Maurras stressed reasoning patriots but also valued will over reason and Catholic order as social mortar.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Exclusion of foreigners from the national community implies reserving benefits, inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Social policy details are not documented; paternal Catholic social thought and discipline pull against each other here.

class-collaboration.rationale: National solidarity under the king over class conflict is core to the doctrine; employers and workers as partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defending inherited culture, institutions and tradition is the point of the doctrine.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras saw France as a great power, not as dominated.

workers-nation.rationale: National solidarity over international class identity; opposed internationalist socialism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist order and Catholic family social thought suggest distinct roles; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a defining part; Maurras did not condemn the bourgeoisie.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Maurras rejected scientific racism and favoured state antisemitism based on culture, not racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state expresses the nation and the king stands above classes; Marxist analysis is rejected.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the doctrine; national self-sufficiency and environmental indifference roughly cancel.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Maurras considered Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and metics as unassimilable, so assimilation is not the aim; exclusion is.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anti-France conspiracy thinking is present about internal enemies, but the Great Replacement is anachronistic.

proportional-representation.rationale: Party-based parliamentary representation is rejected as party rule over national interest.

national-mission.rationale: Maurras was defensive and France-centred; classical civilizing pride exists but exporting regimes is not central.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred rejection of feminist structural analysis in a traditionalist hierarchical order.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Maurras's critique of the Republic as rule by party interests against the nation matches this directly.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras rejected scientific racism but eugenics is not documented.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Authority and military power favoured; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Maurras wanted strong state authority on national matters.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras's exclusion was cultural and political rather than racial.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maurras held natural inequality and excluded groups as Anti-France.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Maurras supported empire and opposed dismantling it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; he favoured Catholic cultural primacy and local autonomy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not discussed by Maurras, who prized Catholicism's social role but did not propose legal limits on conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of French doctrine; inferred opposition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Maurras criticized republican secularism and favored Catholicism's national role.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maurras held legitimacy comes from tradition and national necessity, not popular vote.

population-transfer.rationale: Maurras held that Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners could never be integrated, but forced removal is not clearly documented.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Action Francaise used street violence and sought a coup, rejecting non-aggression absolutism.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Darwinian struggle between nations is a feature of some strands (OUN) but not Maurras's core.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Maurras favoured state suppression of enemies of France and supported Vichy; though his own movement was banned in 1936, adherents support banning anti-national parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty theory is not a doctrine of this tradition; liberty framed as slogan.

separated-powers.rationale: Maurras wanted authority at the top and rejected parliamentary checks.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social Catholic paternalism sympathetic, nation-first conflicting.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed; a paternal-rooted-property sympathy is offset by hostility to Republic-era mass policies.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Maurras criticized class-conflict labor laws; corporatism would limit strikes, inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pronatalist; population decline was lamented, so population is not blamed.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine treats Protestants, Jews, Freemasons and foreigners as Anti-France threatening national unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejects democratic leveling and natural inequality.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Maurras accepted wartime censorship and emergency authority as necessary.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation is not covered; emergency state authority supports it while corporate autonomy opposes it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Maurras favoured censorship of enemies yet opposed party rule; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army serves the nation under the king, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Exclusionary stance toward foreigners implies strict naturalization.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Maurras opposed parties; binding discipline is a party feature.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The nation is the highest value; Maurras opposed supranational dilution.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The king as head holds executive authority and military command; the regime is anti-parliamentary.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism's hierarchical model as an example for society.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and valued the Church for politics; the king, not clergy, rules.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Defeatism contradicts nation-first; Maurras demanded victory.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Maurras was a classicist and moral order-oriented; support for censorship is inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not applicable to a hereditary monarchy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Action Francaise backed alliances against Germany.

people-in-arms.rationale: Professional army and national authority; though conscription supported.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Maurras portrayed Catholic rural family life as source of national renewal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Maurras was himself an intellectual attacking intellectual elites; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Classicist valuing of French and Mediterranean civilization; excludes metics.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented in sources; strong authority supports it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and classical rationalist valuing Church politically, not scriptural literalism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation is rooted in twenty centuries of shared life and foreigners cannot integrate; descent is favoured over soil.

minority-language-support.rationale: Maurras favored provincial liberties and Provencal regionalism but a French national frame; split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Protestants and Jews were treated as Anti-France; exemptions unlikely.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Custom, tradition and order are esteemed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; a nation-first doctrine owing nothing to poor countries leans against, but this is inferred only.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns French sovereignty and does not tie independence to property systems.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution from tradition and royal authority, not elected assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Development dictatorship is not discussed; Maurras defended authority for national ends but not specifically for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Humanitarian concerns rank below the nation.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: National independence and military power; anachronistic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state should be a hereditary king.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed; national sovereignty favours state control while anti-democracy favours insulation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-internal debate on which the doctrine has no stake, although it opposed communism altogether.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not part of the doctrine, and nothing indicates a settled view.

collective-defense.rationale: Action Francaise backed alliances against Germany.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Maurras backed Alsace-Lorraine return; not clear on the general principle.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maurras valued the Church independently as social mortar, but Gallican state-national-church tradition adds ambiguity.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king stands above parties as the keystone of national solidarity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Maurras's monarchism was rational and political, not divine; he was an agnostic.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed in the Maurrasian sources; no principle decides it.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inherited tradition and natural inequality; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; national grandeur might favour it but no source speaks to it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Traditional monarchy bound by custom and natural law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Maurras's ideal was a hereditary king with decentralized bodies, which resembles mixed government loosely, but he never framed it so; split.

leader-cult.rationale: Maurras opposed Hitler and praised monarchy, not mass leader cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law details are not documented; traditionalist family doctrine does not settle the custody question.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the doctrine decides whether returning refugees are welcomed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Maurras's nation was defined by historical shared life, not ethnic claims abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Maurras was himself an agnostic valuing Church politically.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of the French Catholic-tradition doctrine.

common-currency.rationale: National sovereignty over supranational monetary union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minorities as Anti-France; cultural autonomy unlikely.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Maurras's sources never discuss minority strategy, apart from refusing integration of Jews and others in France.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: It puts politics, tradition and the nation first and opposes Marxism, so it rejects economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed; corporatism favours organised industry while national solidarity opposes concentrated power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic crisis policy is not addressed; the doctrine gives no clear principle.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women conflict with the hierarchical, traditionalist order Maurras defended, though he wrote nothing directly on this; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement design is anachronistic and not addressed; nation-first scepticism of international rules balances sympathy to labour protection.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive structure under socialism is outside the doctrine, and no source indicates a view.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Action Francaise planned a coup by force.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Maurras's Enquete calls for a traditional, hereditary, anti-parliamentary monarchy, so hereditary right is central.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Placing the nation's own history at the centre of schooling follows from making France the common frame for all political questions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Maurras opposed assimilation but supported empire.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching loyalty and pride toward the nation follows directly from placing the nation above all other values.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: American-style racial preferences are outside Maurras's context; nation-first opposes group remedies but no direct view exists.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed in the sources, and nothing in the doctrine decides it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Maurras did not engage Marxist crisis theory and did not condemn the bourgeoisie, so no firm position is documented.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist economics suggests some self-sufficiency, but a poor-country strategy is outside the doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed as a libertarian question; adherents defended exclusion of groups from the nation but not as private freedom.

elective-rulers.rationale: Maurras's Enquete asks for a monarchy that is traditional and hereditary, and he attacks elected bodies and officials.

minority-veto.rationale: Minority vetoes would defeat the national authority Maurras demanded, so adherents reject them by inference from the doctrine.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A tradition of monarchical constitutional limits exists, but Maurras said nothing on resistance to a king; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Maurras's monarchy was explicitly anti-parliamentary, placing authority in the king rather than in an assembly.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics fall outside the doctrine's concerns and no position can be inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed in the sources, and the doctrine gives no principle to decide it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternal social Catholic tradition of La Tour du Pin.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Maurras's slogan was "Politique d'abord!" (Politics first!), demanding active political engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school style critique is not part of the doctrine, though Maurras criticised democratic culture; no clear view.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties on which integral nationalism has no stake.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not addressed, though national self-reliance resonates with the doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Maurras sought revenge against Germany and recovery of Alsace-Lorraine.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras defended empire and opposed assimilation, and nation-first thinking rejects group-based leadership claims; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Maurras opposed republican ideology and supported Vichy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Maurras opposed both communism and Hitler but equating is not his framing.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographical dispute outside the doctrine's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Keeping inherited monuments and symbols follows from the doctrine's defence of tradition and the national past.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; a traditionalist order does not settle how men's disadvantage should be handled.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in Maurrasian sources and no doctrinal principle decides it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Each nation develops from its history and tradition.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authority and army; royalists courted officers.

paid-care-work.rationale: Family-based care is valued, but state payment of domestic labour is not discussed; split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Maurras's classicism values competence, but he did not discuss civil-service examinations; split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protecting strategic national firms follows from nation-first thinking and national independence, though it is inferred rather than documented.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed; corporate solidarity suggests collective schemes, but this is only inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only on the community's terms conflicts with the rooted, family-held property of social Catholic thought; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Maurras's monarchy was anti-parliamentary and placed financial and executive authority in the crown, not in an assembly.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; he favoured regional Provencal and French.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Modern American civil rights doctrine is outside the sources, and group-remedy logic conflicts with nation-first principles.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Maurras criticized democratic individualism and self-interest.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not discussed; adherents backed national interest broadly, but no source speaks to it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Cold War bloc discipline is anachronistic; nation-first thinking offers no stated view on great-power interventions.

corporate-influence.rationale: Maurras attacked party and moneyed influence in the Republic, but he did not make corporate lobbying a theme; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Maurras blamed foreign influence on the Republic.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; local liberties favour it, while national uniformity opposes local restrictions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not addressed; paternal solidarity may support it but state-run employment conflicts with corporate autonomy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Maurras held republic produced weakness and war risk.

non-intervention.rationale: Maurras put national interest first and supported alliances and intervention for France, but no general rule on intervention is documented.

industrial-unions.rationale: Class unions rejected for corporate organization.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Anti-France Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and metics were said to undermine the nation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The family is an organic foundation of the national order, so removing legal marriage contradicts the doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency rights are not addressed; the doctrine's emphasis on authority and censorship in emergencies implies scepticism.

local-production.rationale: Local economy resonates with provincial liberties and rural life but is not stated as doctrine; split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Maurras's movement was hierarchical and disciplined, with leagues and a press organ, not informal small groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The nation is the supreme political unit, so national constitution and courts take precedence over supranational law.

religious-nation.rationale: Maurras held Catholicism central to French culture but defined nation historically and was agnostic.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Maurras sought revenge on Germany and recovery of lost Alsace-Lorraine, but reunifying divided nations generally is inferred from nation-first principle.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nation is the supreme value and foreign policy must serve French interests alone, so ritual submission to another power is inferred as rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Maurras favoured decentralisation and restoring provincial liberties under a monarchy, so regions keeping their revenue is inferred as acceptable.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Maurras defended property and class collaboration through corporatism; common ownership of the means of production is the socialism he opposed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Action Francaise was counter-revolutionary and fiercely hostile to socialism and communism, treating them as products of democratic decay.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from corporatist, hierarchical economic thinking in which the state does not run services; mixed delivery is not addressed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maurras, though personally agnostic, valued Catholicism as social cement and order rather than as an illusion to be outgrown.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: Maurras accepted private enterprise but blamed liberal individualism and the money power, so he would not credit capitalism as progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its traditional, hierarchical, family-centred social order and anti-egalitarianism.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its Catholic corporatist emphasis on the family and traditional social order as the unit of care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from Maurras's classicism and hostility to foreign influence on French culture; no purge programme is documented.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the nation's interest overrides inherited legal obligations, and the doctrine has no concept of nations within borders holding treaty rights.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: communal property held in common conflicts with its defence of property, hierarchy and the monarchical national state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: it prized provincial traditions in a decentralised monarchy and aimed at assimilation, not majority settlement of minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corporatist class collaboration under a monarchy was offered as an alternative to both liberal capitalism and socialism, though not framed that way explicitly.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Maurras prized national tradition and the inheritance of the dead, so history-based claims are inferred as acceptable; not stated in the sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic to the audit's period; inferred as rejection of denial, with the movement's antisemitism not extending to this claim.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the traditional Catholic moral order the movement defended.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Maurras was anti-parliamentary, treated groups as Anti-France, and accepted force to restore authority.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Maurras, though personally agnostic, valued Catholicism as social cement and would protect it by law; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: With the nation as supreme value, French empire serving France is inferred as consistent; not directly documented.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; outside the movement's concerns.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Maurras sought a monarchy and used Catholicism as an instrument, not a doctrine of removing rulers by religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Maurras rejected democracy and party rule in favour of a hereditary, hierarchical monarchy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement saw class and group division as the harm of republicanism and favoured class collaboration; intersectional framing is inferred as foreign.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's traditionalism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional Catholic moral stance.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement was explicitly of the nationalist right and counter-revolutionary; inferred as rejecting the claim.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's concept is not discussed; inferred as rejected because the movement favoured corporatist class collaboration.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Maurras excluded Protestants, Jews and foreigners from the nation; inferred that Islam would likewise be seen as alien, though not addressed.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Maurras saw authority in the hereditary monarchy and the nation rather than directly in God, though he valued Catholicism socially.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The movement opposed secular republicanism and valued Catholicism's public role, so excluding religious dress is inferred as rejected.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement favoured corporatist class collaboration, not a market-plus-welfare model; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The nation was the supreme value and force was accepted, so abolishing armed forces runs against it.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; economic distribution was not a core concern.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Maurras stressed national interest in foreign policy, but the sources do not give a position on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Maurras's programme is a traditional, hereditary monarchy, which stresses succession within the royal house.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The movement favoured corporatist class collaboration but did not take a documented position on user-owned banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The nation is the supreme value, so foreign lenders' conditions would be resisted; inferred from nation-above-all.

property-franchise.rationale: Maurras attacked universal suffrage and democracy and wanted authority held by a restricted traditional order; property qualification itself is not stated, so inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The doctrine upholds traditional hierarchy and Catholic social order, so the feminist-ecological claim is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

reification.rationale: It rejects class struggle and Marxist analysis in favour of class collaboration, so this concept is not accepted; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Maurras attacked the power of money in the Republic but also opposed liberal rights as such, so adherents would not endorse the point as framed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Maurras wanted a traditional monarchy under fixed institutions and old law, opposing arbitrary republican politics; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Maurras's 'Anti-France' category excluded Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners from the nation, which implies limits on political rights for outsiders though defined by culture and descent.

online-participation.rationale: The doctrine is anti-democratic and the topic is anachronistic; online participation is inferred to be rejected.

open-government-data.rationale: The doctrine favours authority and rejects public accountability to democratic opinion; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Maurras held Catholicism as social cement and excluded Jews and Protestants from the nation; the sources do not discuss marriage law, so this is inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Action francaise ran anti-Jewish campaigns and street agitation, so boycotts are consistent with its practice; no source documents a shop boycott.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Maurras's Enquete sur la monarchie attacks parliament and popular sovereignty and wants hereditary authority, so assemblies of ordinary citizens deciding public questions are rejected.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Maurras, an agnostic, valued Catholicism as traditional social cement, so reworking its doctrine for modern conditions would undermine that function; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Maurras opposed plutocracy as a republican vice but backed hierarchy and property; adherents are split and the sources do not frame it as a liberty question.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from Maurras and Action Francaise valuing hierarchy, tradition and military honour, and holding conservative Catholic morality; not directly sourced.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as social cement even without personal belief, so state-promoted atheism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian stress on order and a strong state; abolition is not discussed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Maurras defined some groups as Anti-France, and held that national unity needs one tradition rather than communal shares.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Maurras favoured La Tour du Pin style paternal social Catholicism, which mixes corporatist and charitable provision; adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: Maurras opposed parliamentary politics wholesale and backed a hereditary monarch; term limits for elected office are not addressed.

vote-delegation.rationale: It rejected democracy and universal suffrage in favour of hereditary monarchy, so delegable voting is opposed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its focus on national continuity and decline; no source addresses extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its counter-revolutionary Catholic traditionalism; the sources do not discuss clergy.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its traditional hierarchical family ideal, which follows La Tour du Pin style social Catholicism; not directly sourced.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Maurras classed foreigners as Anti-France who could never be integrated, so they should not vote.

rent-control.rationale: Corporatist class collaboration defended property and rejected state-imposed economic controls from parliament; inferred, rent law was not addressed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's defence of property and tradition leans against abolition, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Action Francaise ran the Camelots du Roi as a disciplined militant youth wing for the national cause.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Maurras died in 1952 and never addressed nuclear weapons; his stress on national defence points both ways.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National independence and strong self-defence are core to the doctrine, so foreign bases would be opposed; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; a nation-first movement hostile to republican repentance is unlikely to endorse this, inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Corporatist collaboration and defence of property mean ownership income was accepted; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement accepted force and a coup to restore the monarchy and the nation's defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Enquete grounds France's identity in unbroken continuity through its hereditary monarchy.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A traditionalist, Catholic-aligned movement; inferred, as the idea was far outside its time.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; its traditional social order would oppose it, inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nation as the supreme value implies honouring those who die for it; the movement honoured its dead and national heroes.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maurras was an agnostic who valued Catholicism as social cement, and put politics before faith, not as a spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A France-centred doctrine of national territorial unity under a king; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Maurras's 'politics first' held that restoring the monarchy had to precede any national renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's traditionalist Catholic alignment points to male language, inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A traditionalist, anti-modern movement is unlikely to judge scripture this way; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Groups it labelled Anti-France, Protestants, Jews, Freemasons and foreigners, were to be kept from national life and economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: It proposed a decentralised monarchy of historic provinces within one France, not ethnic units; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Maurras wanted class collaboration through corporative bodies under the king, so unions would be subordinate to the national order; inferred from the corporatism in the summary.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Integral nationalism puts the nation above classes and favours class collaboration, so worker rule is not a condition of a good society; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Social Catholic paternalism and a nation-first outlook suggest public hands for local essentials; not directly addressed.

second-chamber.rationale: Maurras's traditional, corporative, decentralized monarchy envisaged representative bodies beside the crown rather than a single elected parliament; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Adherents defended hereditary property and rejected both collectivism and local-community ownership of production; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Maurras favoured decentralization under a sovereign monarch, not confederations of local assemblies holding the decisions; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: La Tour du Pin's social Catholicism, which Maurras's circle leaned toward, backed a just family-supporting wage; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no principle bears clearly on it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no principle bears clearly on it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A nation-supreme, authoritarian-minded movement would not accept untraceable money outside state control; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: The movement prized national order and authority over individual liberties, so anonymous participation is unlikely to be valued; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The nation is the supreme political value above individuals, so the person may be subordinated to the national community.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Catholicism was valued as social cement and civilizational order, though Maurras himself was agnostic; inferred, with adherents divided on sincerity.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Maurras backed provincial liberties yet a sovereign state; adherents are split on whether regional powers are revocable.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; no principle bears clearly on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Traditionalist, rural-rooted counter-revolutionary outlook makes praise of dense cities unlikely; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Maurrassian nationalism was cultural and political, not racial, and prized one national interest over group interests; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in the French nation was central, but Maurras based it on culture and history, not race; adherents are split on the wording.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement accepted force and a coup to restore authority and valued national strength, so a defensive-only rule is unlikely; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Maurras grounded the nation in history, tradition, monarchy and Catholic heritage and excluded groups that spoke French, so language alone does not define it; inferred from that exclusion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Maurras rejected elected parties and universal suffrage entirely, but also treated religious communities as unassimilable; separate electorates are inferred to be rejected as part of the parliamentary system he opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Action Francaise blamed Anti-France groups and foreign powers for weakening the country and saw France as constantly menaced from outside and within, a central theme of its nationalism.

free-public-college.rationale: Maurras's movement defended a Catholic and classical education and did not address university tuition; adherents give no clear position.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the movement distrusted modern democratic state economics and favoured traditional corporate arrangements; environmental taxes are not addressed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Integral nationalism stresses continuity of the nation across generations and inherited tradition, from which a duty to hand on the land is inferred; the environment itself is not addressed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement's traditionalist, Catholic and anti-egalitarian outlook is inferred to oppose giving women's values more weight in politics; the sources do not discuss the question.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the supremacy of the nation, readiness for force and distrust of humanitarian internationalism; disarmament by agreement is the kind of aim Maurras scorned, though not directly cited.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Enquete argues that a hereditary monarchy secures long-term foreign policy, which depends on continuity and discretion rather than public, parliamentary diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic thought centred on corporatist class collaboration and did not address cross-border capital; no clear position is documented.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Maurras wanted a strong authoritative state, but Action Francaise ran its own street force (the Camelots du Roi), so this is inferred from its authoritarianism.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The nation's defence and survival are supreme values for integral nationalism, so refusing to fight would be treason.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from its corporatism: class collaboration through professional bodies, though not union-versus-employer bargaining as such.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State top-ups of wages are not addressed; inferred from hostility to class legislation and a limited paternal state.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not addressed; Maurras blamed republican party rule for waste, but a binding legal limit is not documented.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its nation-first outlook: foreign policy serves French interests, not reordering the world economy for others.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It sought to overthrow the Republic by coup but to restore authority through a traditional monarchy, keeping and strengthening the state apparatus.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: It demanded one traditional national order under the monarchy and rejected experimentation and pluralism as sources of decline.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is anachronistic and not addressed; no position can be inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The nation is the supreme political value above individuals, classes and humanitarian aims, and a heritage passed down the generations.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its social conservatism and opposition to state redistribution beyond paternal duty.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Maurras blamed Paris centralization and favoured decentralization, but the nation is a single organic unity and the colonial framing is not his.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maurras rejected universal rights and the abstract individual of the Revolution, though he held to classical order; inferred and contested.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its authoritarian view of the press as a servant of national order rather than independent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maurras treated Catholicism as the exclusive social cement of France, not one path among equals, though he was personally agnostic.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ruralist, corporatist and paternal-state outlook; farm price support is not an Action francaise theme.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's priority on national defense and independent foreign policy; nuclear arms are anachronistic for the period.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine seeks class collaboration through corporatism and puts the nation above classes, so a separate workers' party is rejected.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's defense of traditional morality and order, and a prohibition fits a strong state.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist family views point against, state-order and French civil-law tradition point toward, so adherents are split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by Maurras; no doctrine on regional language naming, so it is treated as split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the nation and the state outrank individual property claims, and a tort-only regime without agencies runs against its statism.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its decentralized monarchy built on traditional intermediary bodies, which fits a customary advisory role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the principle that the nation outranks the individual and from land-and-heritage traditionalism.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its demand for strong authority and order against republican leniency.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to foreigners as Anti-France and its stress on French cultural unity; assimilation is the likely demand.

missingStatements.text: Hereditary monarchy is a better guarantee of national continuity than any elected government.
missingStatements.rationale: The Enquete argues a hereditary, traditional monarchy alone secures the nation's interest and long-term foreign policy.

missingStatements.text: Some groups within a country, because of their religion, origin or allegiances, can never be genuinely part of its nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Maurras defined Protestants, Jews, Freemasons and foreigners as Anti-France who could not be integrated.

notes: Based on the French Maurrassian strand. Most answers outside nation, authority, monarchy and exclusion are inferred (low confidence) because Maurras wrote mainly on political form. Variants such as the OUN glorified war and terrorism and clashed with churches.
